summary: Rate-limit transition glitch after tier upgrade causing immediate 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer performed a paid-tier upgrade late 2026-03-10 (self-serve to enterprise commit). Immediately after the upgrade completed, bulk ingesters reported widespread HTTP 429s across upload and streaming routes.

Impact:
- ClipStream ingestion pipelines saw >80% of requests return 429 for ~18 minutes.
- Business impact: delayed CDN metadata indexing; billing spike concern.

Observed behavior:
- Requests originating from the new enterprise key started receiving 429s despite console showing quota increased.
- Console usage graphs show quota refresh but gateway counters still indicated old token-bucket state.
- 429 rate-limit headers show X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset far in the future (seems to be stale refill window).

Expected behavior:
- Quota/limit should take effect immediately after paid upgrade, with token bucket refill aligning to the new limit and console reflect the same live counters.

Workaround applied (customer):
- Customer rotated API key to create a fresh token; some traffic resumed but large upload jobs still hit limits due to connection reuse.

Notes on scope:
- Affects a single org/account (ClipStream) in us-east. Not seen across other customers during same window.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start with a self_serve key under heavy ingestion (concurrent upload workers ~200).
2) Upgrade account to enterprise via console (spend/commit) without changing API key.
3) Immediately resume upload workers.
4) Observe a high volume of 429 responses and stale X-RateLimit-* headers from edge.

(Observed consistently when we replayed with a staging upgrade path.)
logs:
[2026-03-10T23:18:02Z] edge-gw-prod us-east 10.12.5.43 POST /v1/uploads 429 X-RateLimit-Limit:1000 X-RateLimit-Remaining:0 X-RateLimit-Reset:1710582000
[2026-03-10T23:18:07Z] billing-service note: upgrade processed for org clipstream (commit_id=PR-4122)
[2026-03-10T23:22:15Z] rate-limiter debug: token-bucket(id=acct-98765) refill-rate=100/sec state=stale-window(last_refill=1710575400)
[2026-03-10T23:28:40Z] support-runbook action: applied temporary quota-bump (ephemeral policy) for acct-98765

Full request/response headers and a sanitized HAR provided in attachment to ticket.
comments: 2026-03-10T23:25:12Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Received initial report from ClipStream. Confirmed upgrade event at 2026-03-10T23:17Z. Reproduced 429s in staging when replaying upgrade path. Escalating to SRE for token-bucket investigation.

2026-03-10T23:40:03Z - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Initial hypothesis: quota-meta sync lag between billing -> quota-service -> edge. Asking infra to check async consumer offsets and any backlog in Kafka partition for quota updates.

2026-03-10T23:52:45Z - infra-oncall (Slack #support): Noted partition 7 lagged ~4.2m; consumer restarted and caught up at 23:57Z. Suspect race where edge continues to use cached refill-window until invalidation event propagated.

2026-03-11T00:05:10Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Applied temporary quota bump while we validate fix; customer reports reduced 429s but still intermittent for long-lived connections. Recommended customer rotate key or reconnect workers as a mitigating step.

2026-03-12T09:15:00Z - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Deployed patch to force quota cache invalidation on billing-upgrade events (github.com/redwood/release/PR-4122). Monitoring for recurrence. Plan: follow up with postmortem and a tracked task to improve upgrade propagation tests.

2026-03-12T11:02:33Z - ClipStream Support Contact (Nina Zhao): Thanks for the temporary bump. Rotating keys reduced errors for short sessions; still seeing occasional 429s for >5 minute uploads. Looking for a timeline for full resolution and invoice assurance.
investigation_notes: Consumer-lag was real: Kafka partition 7 had ~4m lag at time of upgrade which delayed quota-service processing of billing change events.

Edge layer caches refill windows aggressively (optimizes for token-bucket performance) and relies on an invalidation event; current invalidation handshake was dropped when billing message offset lagged.
We reproduced the problem in staging by intentionally delaying quota-update messages and keeping long-lived HTTP/2 connections pinned to proxy nodes with stale metadata.
Risk: rollout of immediate invalidation could increase write load on edge; mitigated by scoped invalidation only for upgrade events and sessions with long-lived connections flagged.
Related to rate-limit implementation decisions called out in Confluence:RateLimit-Runbook and overlaps with SUP-830102 (geo failover accounting).
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: applied ephemeral quota bump and recommended key rotation for long-lived workers. Long-term fix: patch deployed to force cache invalidation on billing-upgrade events (PR-4122). Follow-up actions: create an automated integration test for upgrade propagation and add monitoring alert on billing->quota consumer lag. Finance/sales to confirm billing impact; customer invoice flagged for review.
next_steps: SRE to monitor for 24h post-patch and close if no recurrence.
Create a runbook addition documenting key rotation recommendation during upgrades.
Finance to review invoice for potential credit; CS to follow up with ClipStream by 2026-03-13.
